Definition

What is a Career Journey?

Can't see the video? Watch it here →

Career Journeys is designed as a dedicated space for employees to explore their aspirations, growth, and future opportunities — separate from performance evaluation.

An employee-centered framework

A Career Journey is designed to empower individuals to actively shape their growth, development, and identify future opportunities. Career Journeys put employees in the driver's seat — while the organization provides the tools and support.

Define. Build. Navigate.

It enables employees to define their aspirations, build capabilities, and navigate meaningful experiences across NYU's global ecosystem through clear structures, tools, and organizational partnership.

What makes it different?

Career Journeys are employee-driven, focused on personal growth and readiness — distinct from organizational programmes such as workforce planning or succession planning, which are designed to meet institutional needs.

The framework

Your journey in 4 stages

Embedded in your employee lifecycle — from your first day to your most senior role.
1Discover

Start with you

Understanding where you are today

  • Use Skills Matcher & VIA Character Strengths Survey
  • Reflect on NYUAD core competencies and growth areas
  • Request Gallup Clifton Strengths via L&OD
  • Connect with manager, mentors, and peers for perspective
Discovering Your Strengths Developing Self-Awareness
2Define

Define your direction

What do you want to become?

  • Explore via O*NET Interest Profiler & Holland Code Quiz
  • Align aspirations with your natural strengths
  • Build a clear, motivating vision for your future
Taking Charge of Your Career Finding Your Purpose at Work
3Act

Take action

How will you get there?

  • Build your Career Journey Career Plan with clear goals
  • Find a mentor — learn from others' experiences
  • Use the LinkedIn Learning Career Hub for AI coaching and feedback
  • Leverage stretch assignments and real-world experiences
How to Develop Your Career Plan Being a Good Mentee
4Evolve

Grow continuously

Review, adjust, unlock new opportunities

  • Dedicated career conversations 2–3 times per year
  • Separate from — and complementary to — performance reviews
  • Connected to NYU global network internal mobility
  • Framework reviewed annually by HR leadership
Asking for Feedback as an Employee Cultivating a Growth Mindset
How development actually happens — the 70/20/10 model
70%
Experiences

On-the-job stretch assignments, new projects, cross-functional work, and taking on broader responsibilities.

20%
Relationships

Learning through feedback, mentoring, coaching conversations with your manager, and peer collaboration.

10%
Training

Formal learning — courses, certifications, workshops, and programmes like the LinkedIn Learning Career Hub.

Core competencies

Five dimensions of growth — across all bands

Select a stage to see the exact behaviour expected. Use the framework as a guide for your development conversations.
Core competencies are one part of the picture. Progressing across bands also requires the relevant technical knowledge, qualifications, and experience for your role and function. For example, becoming an HR Business Partner requires the right education and professional background — the competency framework describes how you work, not what you need to qualify for a role.

Roles & responsibilities

Career Journeys succeed when everyone plays their role

Employee-driven growth, enabled by managers, supported by the organization, aligned with NYUAD priorities.
Employees
Own your journey
  • Reflect on strengths, interests, and aspirations
  • Define and update your career direction
  • Actively engage in career conversations and opportunities
Taking Charge of Your Personal & Professional Success
Managers
Enable growth
  • Hold 2–3 dedicated career conversations per year
  • Provide feedback, guidance, and career perspective
  • Create stretch opportunities and support development
Coaching and Developing Employees
Leadership
Champion & role model
  • Promote a culture of growth, mobility, and development
  • Encourage open career conversations across teams
  • Ensure fairness, transparency, and access to opportunity
Leading with Purpose
